The consumer targets `net10.0` with C# `14.0`, despite its .NET 11 RC SDK pin. Playbook’s .NET 10 catalogue has no matching recipe and reports incomplete coverage. I’m checking the .NET 11 recipes for explicit prerequisites and alternatives; that does not establish compatibility with this consumer.

**The current configuration cannot provide a native, language-enforced closed result type.** It can provide a constrained wrapper, but C# 14 will not recognise its three payload types as an exhaustive set.

The consumer fixes:

- `net10.0`, C# `14.0` and warnings as errors in [Consumer.csproj](V:/_worktrees/PlaybookVerification/verify-pin978-c/consumer/Consumer.csproj).
- SDK `11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105`, with roll-forward disabled, in [global.json](V:/_worktrees/PlaybookVerification/verify-pin978-c/consumer/global.json).

The newer SDK does not override the explicit language version or supply .NET 11 contracts to the .NET 10 target. Microsoft also documents C# 15 on older target frameworks as unsupported. [Language compatibility](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/language-versioning).

I retrieved the full connected Playbook recipes `csharp.closed-results` and `csharp.closed-hierarchies`. Their alternatives compare as follows:

1. **Native union:** Best conceptual fit for three unrelated records. Playbook requires **.NET 11 runtime/reference assemblies, SDK 11 and C# 15**. It needs no experimental opt-in, packages or workloads, but violates your framework and language constraints. Default storage remains an unassigned case requiring explicit handling. [Union reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/union).

2. **Native closed hierarchy:** Has the same version prerequisites. It additionally requires an owned inheritance family, with direct descendants in the declaring assembly and sealed leaves to prevent further inheritance. It is appropriate when outcomes need shared inherited members; it is less suitable for retaining unrelated records. [Closed hierarchy reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/closed).

3. **Handwritten typed wrapper:** Playbook’s older approach works with **.NET 10/C# 14**. Three typed constructors or factories can restrict ordinary creation to your three records. However, matching the stored payload still needs null/default handling and a defensive fallback; the compiler cannot enforce exhaustive handling.

**Recommendation:** Preserve the configuration and use the typed wrapper if restricted construction is sufficient. If compiler-enforced exhaustiveness is mandatory, defer the feature: neither retrieved native route meets your constraints.
